verdict.claim: The local-player hold reaches ModelObject slot 13 through the opaque object returned by Actor+0x18 slot 29. In the normal static CharaActor construction path, Actor+0x18 is a RaptureCharacterController whose slot 29 returns a RaptureCharacterProxy backed by a RigidBody position record; both statically known controller vtables use slot 10 to consume queued position operations. The bounded capture did not record the live controller or proxy vtables, so that concrete runtime type chain and its writer cadence remain unproved. The statically identified RigidBody record is shared physics state, so no render-only correction seam is proven.

runtimeObservations.provenance: Maintainer-supplied bounded retail captures from 2026-09-14, each pinned above by SHA-256; the local video is not repository evidence.
facts: Player Y advances at approximately 30 Hz while Present runs near 60 FPS.
The retail 30 FPS limit removes the visible player, nameplate, slope, and camera stepping.
CameraActor update 0x006195D0 runs once per presented frame and CameraActor+0x250 already yields smooth camera world Y at 60 FPS.
The fixed-function D3DTS_VIEW transform remains identity.
The local controlled object and its ModelObject were identified by comparing ModelObject+0x30 with the simultaneous player-state snapshot; the next-closest actor was materially farther away.
The local controlled tick, 0x00A5FF60, 0x00A61620, and 0x00BB7550 each ran once per Present on the captured route.

Across 533 transitions at 60 FPS, source Y changed 493 times and published Y changed 358 times; 135 source-change frames retained the preceding published Y. Across 321 transitions at 30 FPS, the counts were 259, 241, and 18 respectively.
Within each Present ordinal, the local controlled sample preceded 0x00A5FF60, which enclosed 0x00A61620 and 0x00BB7550.

Three exactly matched vertex-constant tasks used start register 0 and count 16 on observed player-draw frames; they ran before that ordinal's update and consumed a previously published drawable transform.
The local ModelObject did not enter 0x008DEC70, although its cached transform changed inside 0x00A5FF60 before drawable publication.
NamePlate+0x78..+0x84 and +0x98..+0xA4 did not change during either movement segment.
The follow-up capture identified the live local ModelObject vtable as 0x010653A4 and confirmed slots 7, 13, 25, and 26 as 0x00A61620, 0x008DE970, 0x008DE790, and 0x008DEC70.
Actor+0x18 was non-null, Actor+0x48 was non-null, and (Actor+0x48)+0x20 was null, proving that the local callback took the fallback slot-13 branch.

Across 436 aligned 60 FPS transitions, ModelObject+0x30 Y changed 400 times and drawable Y changed 297 times. On all 103 source-change/publication-hold frames, slot 13 received the preceding published Y and copied it over the newer ModelObject+0x30 Y.
Slot 25 rebuilt the cached transform after slot 13 and supplied the exact record passed to the Drawable setter; it did not introduce the held Y.
runtimeObservations.consequence: CameraActor, D3DTS_VIEW, aspect ratio, navmesh, collision, server movement, packets, and authoritative actor coordinates are outside this correction investigation.

proven: Actor+0x0C owns the ModelObject used by both CharaActor slot 34 and UPDATE_MODEL_TRANSFORM.
CharaActor slot 34 returns the [X, Y, Z, 1] record at ModelObject+0x30 to the controlled-actor tick.
The live local ModelObject vtable was 0x010653A4. Its slots 7, 13, 25, and 26 resolved to 0x00A61620, 0x008DE970, 0x008DE790, and 0x008DEC70.
Actor+0x48 was non-null but its +0x20 member was null, so the local 0x00A5FF60 callback took the Actor+0x18 fallback and never called slot 26.

The normal CharaActor slot-68 path constructs a RaptureCharacterProxy and a RaptureCharacterController, stores the proxy at controller+0x04, and stores the controller at Actor+0x18. The bounded capture did not record the live controller vtable, but both known base and Rapture controller vtables use 0x00A68000 for slot 10 and 0x008D5570 for slot 29.

On both statically known controller vtables, slot 10 dispatches the queued operation selected by controller+0x0C and clears the selector. Slot 29 returns controller+0x04; in the normal static construction path this is the CharacterProxy supplied to 0x00A61130.

0x00A61130 reads +0x2C from the opaque slot-29 result and copies its active indexed position record through 0x00AFA220. Static construction identifies this as CharacterProxy+0x2C RigidBody, but the live vtables were not captured. The reader contains no previous/current selection, interpolation, or cadence gate.
The active record address is **(RigidBody+0x14) + (RigidBody+0x10 * 0x70). Direct writer 0x00AFA160 updates [X, Y, Z, 1] at record+0x00 and clears record+0x64.

For the statically constructed RaptureCharacterProxy vtable, queued states 1 and 2 reach slot 1 at 0x007D8080 and queued state 3 reaches slot 2 at 0x007D8E90. Both paths can call 0x00AFA160; state zero writes nothing and preserves the prior RigidBody position.

Actor slot 32 at 0x00A5F810 queues an absolute value through controller slot 7 before ModelObject slot 16 at 0x008DDAB0 writes the same four lanes to ModelObject+0x30. This is the earliest static path that establishes both copies, but it does not prove the local runtime writer or when slot 10 consumes the queue.
Static slot 13 writes shared ModelObject+0x30 and either invalidates the cached transform for slot-25 rebuild or mirrors the four-float record directly to four lanes at +0x80..+0x8C.

When its drawable and dirty-bit guards pass, ModelObject slot 7 obtains the cached record, optionally transforms it under bit 0x10, and copies the resulting record to drawable+0x30..+0x6C through 0x00BB7550.

On every observed hold frame, the old Y was already present in the slot-13 input. Therefore the hold is introduced before 0x00A61130 returns, not by ModelObject slot 13, slot 25, or drawable publication.
unresolved: The capture did not record the live Actor+0x18 or CharacterProxy vtables, although the normal CharaActor construction path and both known controller variants agree on slots 10 and 29.

Static evidence cannot determine whether CharacterController+0x0C is zero on held frames, which queue setter supplied each changing frame, or whether another CharacterProxy/RigidBody writer ran between the queue and 0x00A5FF60.
No static timer or frame divider was found in slot 10, 0x00A61130, 0x00AFA220, or 0x00AFA160. The approximately 30 Hz producer cadence is a runtime question, not a promoted static fact.
Fields outside record+0x00..+0x0F, +0x64..+0x65, and +0x6C..+0x6F do not have proven previous/current, target/current, keyframe, accumulator, or timing semantics.
The indexed record has statically identified physics readers and writers. No direct packet, gameplay-authority, collision-response, or NamePlate consumer is established by the retained evidence.
The trace matched register-0/count-16 player-draw tasks to previously published drawable state, but the exact task object and static data-flow edge remain unresolved.

namePlateFlow.proven: CharaElement per-actor tick 0x0058DF90 invokes slot 19 and then slot 13 on the inline NamePlate subobject at CharaElement+0xBA0. Slot 19 at 0x006A2A60 only updates bit 0x04 at NamePlate+0x190. Slot 13 synchronizes presentation state and index-1 RGBA color; the captured +0x78/+0x98 records remained constant during movement. After slot 13, 0x00796D50 reads and copies two opaque records and calls 0x00923FE0, while 0x00797FE0 updates a countdown popup. NamePlate is not a Sqwt FrameworkElement; +0x194 is an opaque pointer used by UI helpers.
namePlateFlow.unresolved: No static edge identifies which object stores or publishes the moving screen-space anchor. The +0x78/+0x98 color records are excluded, but slot 13 still reaches indirect helpers 0x006A2D50 and 0x006A2E90 whose downstream writes have not been fully resolved. The presentation effect of 0x00796D50, plus NamePlate+0x194 ownership and relevance, remains unresolved.

records: At 0x00A5FF60 entry, identify the local Actor dynamically by comparing Actor+0x0C ModelObject+0x30 against the simultaneous player-state snapshot, using the same match method as the retained capture; persist that Actor and ModelObject only for this run. Record Present ordinal, thread id, Actor+0x18, *(Actor+0x18), controller+0x0C, +0x10..+0x1C, controller+0x04, *(controller+0x04), and ModelObject+0x30..+0x3C.

At 0x00A68000 entry and return, filter ECX to the Actor+0x18 value recorded above. Record Present ordinal, return address, +0x0C, +0x10..+0x1C, controller+0x04, and the candidate +0x2C active record before and after the call.

At 0x00A61130 entry, require the enclosing local 0x00A5FF60 call and record Present ordinal, thread id, ECX, *(ECX), [ESP+4], ECX+0x2C, and the active [X,Y,Z,1] record. Use this observed ECX as the slot-29 result and this observed +0x2C value as the writer filter; do not derive either from controller+0x04.

At 0x007D8080 and 0x007D8E90 entry, filter ECX to the controller+0x04 candidate recorded at the enclosing local 0x00A5FF60 entry and set a per-thread dispatch marker. Record Present ordinal, target VA, caller return address, and input lanes; retain the event only when the later 0x00A61130 ECX for that callback matches the candidate. Consume and clear the marker at the first matching 0x00AFA160 entry; clear it unconsumed on the ordinary wrapper return or the 0x007D8E90 null-RigidBody return. This lets the marker survive the 0x007D8E90 tail jump without leaking to a later write.

At 0x00AFA160 entry, filter ECX to the +0x2C value observed at 0x00A61130. Record Present ordinal, thread id, return address, the consumed proxy dispatch marker, the four input lanes at [ESP+4], and the active record before the call; retain a separate per-call hook context to record the same record after return. A single short 60 FPS slope traversal is sufficient.
runtimeProbe.successCriteria: On each of the already defined source-change/publication-hold frames, establish the live controller and returned-object vtables, determine whether controller+0x0C was zero, whether slot 10 changed the indexed record, and which exact 0x00AFA160 caller or marked tail-dispatch last wrote that record. This distinguishes an unqueued hold from an opaque-helper-mediated write or an earlier consumer without a broad trace.
runtimeProbe.currentBestSeam: No correction seam is proven. The normal static CharacterController, CharacterProxy, and RigidBody path is shared scene/physics state, and live ModelObject slot 13 overwrites the shared ModelObject+0x30 record. Drawable publication remains downstream, but absence of feedback and the moving NamePlate consumer are not proven.

ownershipBoundary.authoritative: The live slot-13 target 0x008DE970 overwrites ModelObject+0x30, which the controlled-actor path samples. In the normal static construction path, its upstream record is CharacterProxy+0x2C RigidBody state consumed and written by physics methods; the live type chain remains to be captured. Neither proven boundary is render-only, and this evidence does not authorize changing actor, collision, packet, server, or gameplay state.
ownershipBoundary.renderCandidate: Drawable+0x30..+0x6C is downstream of ModelObject publication and feeds later draw tasks, but negative feedback into shared state and the moving NamePlate consumer are not proven.
ownershipBoundary.launcherDisposition: Do not implement interpolation. If further runtime work is authorized, limit it to the five exact filtered observations above.
